criteria.text: Diagnosis of relapsing remitting multiple sclerosis only (approval 2; denial 1)
Inadequate response to at least 2 medications FDA-indicated for MS (approval 3; denial 3)
All parties meet Lemtrada REMS requirements, including on-site infusion-reaction equipment and trained personnel (approval 4a–4e; denial 4)
Baseline labs acceptable under REMS requirements; results submitted with PA request (approval 4f)
Administering provider enrolled with Alaska Medicaid as a Health Professional Group or Medical provider (physician or APRN) (approval 5; denial 7)
Not administered under Alaska Medicaid Home Infusion Therapy program (approval 6; denial 8)
Not used in combination with another MS disease-modifying agent (approval 7; denial 5)
Negative HIV test before treatment (approval 8; denial 2)
Negative tuberculosis test before treatment (approval 8; denial 6)

notes: Partial encoding of Alaska Medicaid Lemtrada (alemtuzumab), a CD52-directed cytolytic monoclonal antibody. Version: 1; Last updated: 3/3/2016; Approved: 3/25/2016; Effective: 10/3/2016.
Encoded: initial approval criteria 1–8 and denial criteria 1–8. RRMS is the only accepted diagnosis. No numeric age requirement is stated in the criteria; no age gate is encoded.

REMS attestation (4a–4e): prescriber certified through enrollment and completed training; patient enrolled and compliant with ongoing monitoring; dispensing pharmacy certified and dispensing only to certified healthcare facilities authorized to receive Lemtrada; healthcare facility enrolled and verifying patient authorization before infusion; facility has on-site equipment and personnel trained to manage infusion reactions. All five requirements must be met.

REMS baseline labs (4f): lab tests deemed acceptable under REMS requirements, with results submitted with the prior authorization request. These and prior therapy requirements are attestations; documentation requires manual review.
Concurrent MS DMT examples: interferon beta preparations (Avonex, Betaseron, Extavia, Plegridy, Rebif), glatiramer acetate (Copaxone, Glatopa), and dimethyl fumarate (Tecfidera).
Duration (notes only): initial coverage up to 1 year; reauthorization up to 1 year.

Reauthorization (notes only): all initial criteria must still be met, with documented positive clinical response and current labs acceptable under REMS continuation requirements; lab documentation must be submitted.
Quantity (notes only): initial authorization 5 vials (6 mL); subsequent reauthorizations 3 vials (3.6 mL). Strength: 12 mg/1.2 mL (10 mg/mL) single-use vial. No numeric quantity enforcement.

Mechanism and safety (notes only): precise MS mechanism unknown; presumed CD52 binding followed by antibody-dependent cellular cytolysis and complement-mediated lysis of T and B lymphocytes. Because of its safety profile, generally reserved for inadequate response to two or more MS drugs.
PDL status unknown: PDF is silent. Alternatives are encoded MS disease-modifying peers and require separate eligibility evaluation.
Remaining gaps: documentation verification, reauthorization, authorization duration, dosing and quantity enforcement require manual review.
